samples.summary: `--rebuttals` parse failure echoes raw file bytes to the terminal without `printable()`, re-opening the ANSI-injection hole this file documents
samples.evidence: The delta restructures this block so `JSON.parse(readFileSync(file,"utf8"))` sits alone in the `try`, and the catch interpolates `e.message` verbatim: `throw new Error("--rebuttals file is not a readable JSON array: " + file + " (" + e.message + ")")` (spec-to-pr.mjs:706-709). That error reaches the terminal unfiltered via `fail(e.message)` at spec-to-pr.mjs:1151 (real run) and :1124 (dry run). On Node 20+ V8 embeds a snippet of the INPUT in the SyntaxError — `JSON.parse("[2Jnope")` yields `Unexpected token ... "<raw bytes>" is not valid JSON` — so a rebuttals file whose first ~30 bytes are ESC/CSI sequences gets those bytes printed raw. Attack: the rebuttals file on this path is commonly written by the fixer agent / model output about the branch under review, i.e. the party under review; a crafted file that fails to parse can clear the screen or overwrite the blocking-findings report a developer is reading to decide the branch is clean. That is exactly the threat `printable()` (spec-to-pr.mjs:274-296) exists for — every other model-sourced string printed by this command goes through it; this error string does not. Also applies to the new `record(s) no lens can adjudicate` message at :715, though its interpolated parts (path from argv, static reasons) are less attacker-shaped.

samples.summary: The new checkout/branch store key is a 32-bit truncated SHA-1, so the docblock's "cannot share a slot" guarantee is brute-forceable
samples.evidence: `reviewBase` now derives the store slot as `sha1(`${repo}\n${branch}`).slice(0,8)` — 32 bits — and the docblock above it (spec-to-pr.mjs:816-838) rests the whole isolation argument on that hash: "hashed so two branch names that sanitize to the same string cannot share a slot" / "distinct per clone and per `git worktree`". A 32-bit truncation is trivially collidable (seconds of brute force), and `safe` collapses every ref-legal punctuation char (`%`, `+`, `=`, `,`, `@`, `!`, `#`, `$`, `&`, `(`, `)`, `'`, `/`) to `-`, so an attacker who controls a branch name in a repo a developer clones has a large space of names that render the SAME readable half. A collision puts two contexts in one store, and the consequence is the one the docblock itself names: `priorFindingsFor` (spec-to-pr.mjs:928) reads the other context's `verdict.json` and feeds that text into this round's verifier prompt — model-written text derived from a diff the attacker wrote. I could not build a working collision (that would need the victim's exact repo path), so confidence is low; the fix is cheap: sha256 and a longer slice, and include `process.getuid()`.

samples.summary: The store key namespaces by checkout but not by user; `<tmp>/wafflebase-self-review` stays a globally shared name any local user can squat, wedging the tool fail-closed
samples.evidence: `reviewBase` returns `path.join(os.tmpdir(), "wafflebase-self-review", `${safe}-${hash}`)` — the parent segment is a fixed, unprivileged, world-predictable name in a shared `/tmp` with no uid component, even though this delta is specifically a redesign of what the store is keyed on. Consequences a local unprivileged attacker gets for free: (a) pre-create `/tmp/wafflebase-self-review` as themselves (any mode) — the developer's `mkdirSync(requested,{recursive:true,mode:0o700})` at :1016 either fails EACCES into `fail("...it could not be created")` or succeeds and is then refused by the ancestor rule at :1055-1056 (`owned by uid N, neither root nor M`); either way `spec-to-pr review` never runs again on that machine until someone manually clears /tmp, and the refusal message points at a directory the developer did not create. (b) Two legitimate users on one build host or shared dev box cannot both use the tool, for the same reason. The guard fails closed, which is why this is minor rather than an integrity bug, but a uid (or `mkdtemp`-per-user) segment in the parent removes the squattable name entirely and costs nothing.

samples.summary: `blockingFindingsIn` builds a filesystem path from an unvalidated `panel.json` id (path traversal, defence-in-depth)
samples.evidence: Newly exported and newly exercised end-to-end by this delta, `blockingFindingsIn(outDir, lensIds)` does `readFileSync(path.join(outDir, lens, "verdict.json"))` where `lens` comes straight from `panel.json`: `blockingFindingsIn(outDir, blocking.map((p) => p.id))` at spec-to-pr.mjs:1203, with `blocking` filtered out of `JSON.parse(readFileSync(path.join(outDir,"panel.json")))` at :1195 and no check that the id is a known lens. An id of `../../../../home/victim/.config/something` would make the command read and render a JSON file outside the round directory; its `findings[].summary` would then be printed by `renderBlockingFindings`. Impact is bounded because `outDir` lives under the 0700-guarded base and `panel.json` is written by the spawned panel from the lens manifest (review-panel.mjs:3181), so an attacker able to control it can already write in that directory — hence low confidence and minor severity. Cheap hardening: intersect the ids with the lens directory names actually present, or reject any id that is not `[a-z0-9-]+`, the same discipline `roundsIn`/`ROUND_DIR_RE` applies to round names.

finding.summary: The round store is keyed on the branch NAME alone, so two checkouts with the same branch name share one carry-forward store — the exact cross-context prompt-injection channel `branchKey` was written to close for detached HEAD
finding.evidence:
`reviewBase(branch)` (spec-to-pr.mjs:771-775) derives the base from the branch string only: `path.join(os.tmpdir(), "wafflebase-self-review", `${safe}-${hash}`)`, where `hash = sha1(branch)`. Nothing in the key identifies the repository, worktree, or remote — `cmdReview` calls it as `reviewBase(branch)` at line 902 with `branch = branchKey(git rev-parse --abbrev-ref HEAD, …)`.

`branchKey`'s own docblock (lines 737-753) states the harm precisely for the detached-HEAD case: sharing a key means the checkouts "share a round counter … and, far worse, one carry-forward store — `priorFindingsFor` would read another change's verdicts and put their text into this round's verifier prompt." That harm is unaddressed for the much more common collision: two clones/worktrees on the same branch name.

Attack: a contributor controls both their branch NAME and its diff content. A maintainer who clones/worktrees the contributor's branch beside their own work — or simply has two checkouts on a common name such as `main`/`dev` — gets one shared base. `priorFindingsFor` (line 860-870) then reads `<base>/round-N/<lens>/verdict.json` written while reviewing the OTHER checkout and hands it to `prepareRoundInputs` → `panelArgs --prior-findings` (lines 1055-1062, 1086-1095), i.e. straight into the next round's verifier prompt. Lens verdict text is model output derived from the hostile diff, so a contributor who names their branch to collide can place chosen text in front of an agent session running in the maintainer's other checkout. The same collision also lets one checkout's rounds consume the other's three-round bound.

The per-user 0700 base limits this to a single user's checkouts, which is why this is `major` rather than `critical`. Fix: fold the repository identity (e.g. `git rev-parse --show-toplevel`, or the `origin` URL) into the hash alongside the branch.

verdict.reason:
The code is not as described. `reviewBase` in the working tree takes the checkout root as a second key component and folds it into the hash: `scripts/agent/spec-to-pr.mjs:839-843` — `export function reviewBase(branch, repo = "")` with `createHash("sha1").update(`${String(repo)}\n${String(branch)}`)`. The reviewer's quoted body (`hash = sha1(branch)` only, at lines 771-775) does not exist anywhere in the file.

The sole production call site supplies the repo half: `scripts/agent/spec-to-pr.mjs:984-993` resolves `repoRoot` from `git rev-parse --show-toplevel`, `realpathSync`-normalises it (so two paths to one checkout collapse to one key, and distinct clones/worktrees get distinct keys), falls back to `process.cwd()` when git cannot answer, and then calls `reviewBase(branch, repoRoot)`. A repo-wide grep for `reviewBase(` finds no other caller besides tests (`scripts/agent/spec-to-pr.test.mjs:562-571`, which assert exactly that two checkouts on branch `main` get different bases and that the base is stable per checkout).

The docblock at lines 815-838 explicitly addresses the same-branch-name-across-checkouts collision the finding claims is unaddressed ("AND KEYED BY THE CHECKOUT, not the branch alone…"), and the fix the finding recommends (fold `git rev-parse --show-toplevel` into the hash) is precisely what the code already does. Consequently the claimed carry-forward cross-contamination path (`priorFindingsFor` at 928-938 reading another checkout's `verdict.json` into `--prior-findings`) cannot be reached by a branch-name collision alone. The only residual is the `repo = ""` default parameter, which no live caller uses — a hygiene/design point, not an exploitable security defect.
